*leans against the wall, studying the code*

Look, this URL validation thing... it's like the game, man. You got rules, but sometimes the rules got holes in 'em. People slip through.

## Root Cause Analysis

The pawns here are the username and password fields in URLs. RFC 1738 says certain characters - `:`, `@`, `/` - gotta be encoded when they're in those fields. But the regex? It just lets 'em through raw.

Check `django/core/validators.py`. The URLValidator regex pattern accepts usernames and passwords, but it ain't checking if special characters are properly %-encoded. So `http://foo/bar@example.com` slides through when it shouldn't - that `/` in "foo/bar" ain't encoded.

## Proposed Fix

*scratches head*

This is the game. We gotta tighten up that user/password portion of the regex:

```python
# In django/core/validators.py

@deconstructible
class URLValidator(validators.RegexValidator):
    ul = '\u00a1-\uffff'  # Unicode letters range
    
    # The fix - encode-safe characters only for user:password
    # Exclude : @ / from the allowed unencoded characters
    user_pass = r'[^\s:@/]+'  # Characters that don't need encoding
    # Or more precisely, allow alphanumerics, %-encoded sequences, and safe specials
    user_pass = r'(?:[a-zA-Z0-9._~!$&\'()*+,;=-]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+'
    
    # Update the regex pattern to use this restricted character class
    # for the userinfo portion before the @
```

The current pattern probably looks something like `[^\s:@]+` or similar for matching usernames - but `/` ain't excluded. We need:

```python
# Userinfo should only allow:
# - Unreserved chars: A-Za-z0-9-._~
# - Percent-encoded: %XX
# - Sub-delims: !$&'()*+,;=
# - And colon only between user:password, not inside them
```

## Test Considerations

*sits down on the steps*

Sometimes I wonder if we really testing everything we building here.

Add to `tests/validators/invalid_urls.txt`:
```
http://foo/bar@example.com
http://user:pass/word@example.com
http://user@name:password@example.com
http://us:er:password@example.com
```

Add to `tests/validators/valid_urls.txt`:
```
http://foo%2Fbar@example.com
http://user:pass%2Fword@example.com
http://user%40name:password@example.com
```

Then run:
```bash
python -m pytest tests/validators/tests.py -k URLValidator
```

---

*stares off*

You know what gets me though? Every time you tighten the rules, some legit URL someone's been using gonna break. The pawns always get capped first. But if the RFC says encode them characters, that's the game we playing. Can't be letting invalid URLs through just 'cause it's easier.

The game is the game. We implement what's right.
